edges.description: Monoclonal plasma cells and the reactive marrow microenvironment upregulate intracellular IL-6 and systemic TNF-alpha and IL-12 signaling.
Bone marrow plasma cells and associated microenvironment overexpress VEGF mRNA and secrete markedly elevated circulating VEGF.
Focal or multifocal clonal plasma cell lesions induce osteoblastic new bone formation, producing sclerotic or mixed lytic-sclerotic bone lesions.
Paraneoplastic cytokine signaling associated with the clonal plasma cell disorder drives reactive thrombocytosis in approximately half of patients.
The clonal plasma cell paraneoplastic milieu promotes erythrocytosis rather than the anemia typical of multiple myeloma.
Focal osteoblastic bone deposition manifests radiographically as densely osteosclerotic or sclerotic-rimmed bone lesions.
Elevated IL-6 and allied proinflammatory cytokines induce VEGF expression and secretion by plasma cells and stromal/osteoblastic cells.
Proinflammatory cytokines act in concert with VEGF to impair endothelial barrier integrity and promote systemic capillary leak.
Upregulated proinflammatory and proangiogenic cytokines cooperate with VEGF to drive pathological microvascular proliferation.
Systemic paraneoplastic cytokine excess (including IL-6) promotes hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and Castleman-spectrum lymphadenopathy.
Paraneoplastic cytokine and angiogenic factor dysregulation contributes to pulmonary vascular remodeling and elevated pulmonary arterial pressure.
Paraneoplastic systemic cytokine dysregulation impairs multiple endocrine axes through unresolved intermediates.
Paraneoplastic cytokine excess is associated with gonadal axis suppression, the most frequent endocrine abnormality in POEMS syndrome.
Central pituitary hormone axis dysfunction arises through unresolved paraneoplastic neuroendocrine intermediates.
Adrenal axis impairment occurs within the paraneoplastic multiorgan endocrine spectrum of POEMS syndrome.

Overexpressed VEGF contributes to endoneurial endothelial activation, opening tight junctions and disrupting the blood-nerve barrier alongside other angiogenic and inflammatory mediators; however, selective VEGF blockade alone with bevacizumab does not reliably reverse neuropathy and has worsened disease in several cases.

edges.description: Systemic VEGF excess acts with cooperating cytokines to increase microvascular permeability and drive third-space capillary leak, although isolated VEGF neutralization with bevacizumab can paradoxically precipitate clinical deterioration and capillary leak rather than durable control.
Elevated circulating VEGF stimulates endothelial receptor signaling and pathological dermal and systemic angiogenesis in concert with other angiogenic factors.
Blood-nerve barrier leakage and secondary ischemic microangiopathy cause uncompacted myelin demyelination and progressive axonal degeneration.

edges.description: Intermediate-segment demyelination and distal axonal loss manifest clinically as progressive symmetric sensorimotor polyradiculoneuropathy.
Systemic capillary hyperpermeability causes peripheral interstitial fluid transudation and third-space volume overload.
Peritoneal microvascular hyperpermeability causes third-space ascitic fluid accumulation.
Pleural capillary leak produces pleural effusions.
Optic nerve head microvascular hyperpermeability and elevated intracranial fluid pressure produce bilateral papilledema.
Microvascular barrier dysfunction and extravascular volume overload accompany pulmonary arterial hypertension in advanced POEMS syndrome.
Dermal angiogenesis and paraneoplastic cytokine signaling produce glomeruloid hemangiomas, cutaneous angiomas, hyperpigmentation, hypertrichosis, and skin thickening.
Serum and plasma VEGF concentration directly measures systemic VEGF excess and decreases with effective anti-plasma-cell treatment.
Lambda-restricted IgA or IgG paraprotein reports the presence of the underlying clonal plasma cell disorder.

nodes.description: POEMS syndrome originates from a somatic clonal plasma cell proliferation in bone marrow or focal plasmacytoma lesions, almost invariably expressing a lambda light-chain-restricted IgA or IgG monoclonal immunoglobulin with highly restricted IGLV1-44 or IGLV1-40 germline usage, frequent 14q32 (IGH) translocations and 13q14 deletions, and a heterogeneous somatic mutational profile. Unlike classic multiple myeloma, clonal plasma cell burden is typically low, yet eradication of the clone reverses the paraneoplastic syndrome.
